tz.headline: CHRAGG calls for dialogue after Lissu conviction
tz.dek: The Commission for Human Rights and Good Governance says disputes over the ruling belong in lawful channels, not the street.
paragraphs: Four years in prison: that is the sentence the High Court in Dar es Salaam handed Tundu Lissu, chairman of the opposition party CHADEMA, after it acquitted him of treason on November 6 but convicted him of incitement. The Commission for Human Rights and Good Governance (CHRAGG) has now urged respect for judicial independence and constructive dialogue over the case.

In a position statement issued in Dodoma on November 13, the commission said disagreements over the judgment should be pursued through the constitution and through lawful, democratic channels. It said it had no power to review or overturn the court's findings. Its records showed Lissu's arrest on April 9, 2025, his appearance before the Kisutu Resident Magistrates' Court the next day, and his committal and trial all followed the criminal procedure framework.

CHRAGG cautioned that following procedure is not the same as meeting every human rights duty, and pointed to access to a lawyer and time to prepare a defence. An inquiry it opened on June 27, 2025 found Lissu had freedom of worship, privacy, contact with his legal team and exercise while in custody. The commission added that peaceful calls for constitutional and electoral reform must be kept separate from criminal conduct.

tz.headline: Tanzania reports clean-cooking gains
tz.dek: President Samia Suluhu Hassan said Tanzania expects clean-cooking access to reach 35 per cent by the end of 2026.
paragraphs: President Samia Suluhu Hassan reported an expansion in clean-cooking access, stating Tanzania expects it to reach 35 per cent by the end of 2026. Leaders at COP31 urged that international pledges be measured by improvements in households’ lives. Discussions reviewed progress since the 2024 Paris clean-cooking summit, which mobilised US$2.2 billion in commitments, with approximately US$740 million deployed.

President Samia said access in Tanzania increased from 16 per cent in 2022 to 28.6 per cent in March 2024, attributing progress to rural electrification, reduced electricity tariffs, and subsidies for liquefied petroleum gas equipment. By March 2026, the government had distributed over 346,000 subsidised LPG cylinders and 49,000 induction stoves. The Cook Fund programme enabled over 413,000 households, nearly two million people, to gain access to clean-cooking solutions.

The Cook Fund programme supported hundreds of local businesses and 45 public institutions, including schools serving more than 62,000 students. Interventions contributed to an estimated reduction of 3.8 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent emissions. President Samia pledged to strengthen the national clean-cooking strategy through appropriate technologies, better distribution networks, and greater private investment, particularly in rural areas.

tz.headline: Tanzania's Works ministry orders better data for construction projects
tz.dek: The ministry wants its agencies to improve how they collect and analyse data to track public spending and project results.
paragraphs: The Ministry of Works has told directors and monitoring and evaluation managers in its supervised institutions to improve data collection and analysis. The call was made by Veila Shoo, director of the ministry's Monitoring and Evaluation Unit, when she closed a first-quarter meeting in Dodoma.

Shoo said accurate data lets the government make informed decisions, monitor public funds and assess outcomes in the construction sector. "We cannot achieve Vision 2050 without accurate data," she said, adding that every shilling spent on construction must be monitored. The meeting brought together the Tanzania National Roads Agency (TANROADS), the Tanzania Buildings Agency (TBA), the Engineers Registration Board (ERB) and the Contractors Registration Board (CRB), among others.

Participants discussed the sector's role in the National Development Vision 2050, the management of national plans and the state of monitoring and evaluation. They were also urged to prioritise strategic infrastructure projects, including roads and modern buildings, in line with long-term development goals.

tz.headline: Africa experts push digital tech against fake seeds
tz.dek: African agricultural experts met in Dar es Salaam to discuss using digital technology and biotechnology to improve seed quality and food security.
paragraphs: African agricultural experts are advocating for increased use of digital technology to combat counterfeit seeds, which threaten farmers' productivity and food security. This proposal emerged from the Seventh Steering Group Meeting of the African Seed and Biotechnology Partnership Platform, organised by AUDA-NEPAD and held in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, on November 12, 2026.

Dr James Onsando, an adviser on seed sector issues, stated that digital authentication systems could help farmers identify genuine seeds from fake ones, often sold in imitative packaging. He explained that concealed verification codes on seed packages would allow farmers to confirm authenticity, protecting them from financial losses due to poor germination and harvests from counterfeit seeds.

Delegates also explored biotechnology's role in developing higher-yielding seed varieties resilient to climate change, pests, and diseases. However, expanding access requires investment in research, supportive policies, and regulatory frameworks. These discussions align with the Comprehensive Africa Agriculture Development Programme's 2026–2035 agenda, which aims to significantly increase agricultural production and investment across the continent.

ma.headline: Wafa Assurance acquires La Marocaine Vie from Saham Group
ma.dek: The deal includes a long-term bancassurance partnership allowing Saham Bank to continue offering insurance products through its network.
paragraphs: Wafa Assurance has signed an agreement to acquire 99.98% of the capital of La Marocaine Vie from the Saham Group. This transaction aims to strengthen Wafa Assurance's position in life insurance, savings, and retirement services within the Moroccan market.

The agreement includes a long-term commercial partnership between Wafa Assurance and Saham Bank. This arrangement ensures that Saham Bank clients can continue to access insurance solutions through their existing bank branches while the two companies develop new joint offerings.

ma.headline: Colas Rail wins €29 million Moroccan rail contract
ma.dek: The French firm will carry out track, catenary and civil engineering works in the Casablanca area for the Kenitra–Marrakesh high-speed line.
paragraphs: Morocco's National Railways Office (ONCF) has awarded French firm Colas Rail a 29 million euro contract for the Kenitra–Marrakesh high-speed rail project. The work covers track, catenary and civil engineering between Roches-Noires station and the Nouaceur Technicentre in the Casablanca area.

Hervé Le Joliff, Colas Rail's executive vice president for railways, said Morocco is a strategic market and that the contract reaffirms the company's commitment to high-speed rail in the Kingdom. Colas Rail has operated in Morocco for more than 17 years and employs around 550 staff.

The company is already working on the same line under two contracts secured in January 2025, worth 250 million euros in total. Its Moroccan teams have carried out more than 40 projects across the country, including several modernisation programmes on the rail network.

ma.headline: Casablanca police arrest 15-year-old over false school bomb threat
ma.dek: Police say the teenager made two anonymous calls on Friday falsely threatening a car bomb outside a Casablanca school.
paragraphs: Moroccan police arrested a 15-year-old student in Casablanca on Friday on suspicion of making a false report of a terrorist threat against schools in the city, the General Directorate of National Security (DGSN) said. The arrest was carried out by the Casablanca Judicial Police Brigade with the General Directorate for Territorial Surveillance (DGST) on November 13.

A school in Casablanca received two calls on Friday morning from an unidentified number, in which the caller threatened to detonate a car bomb in front of the building. Security services activated emergency safety procedures for serious threats. Investigators later established the threats were fabricated and that a minor was allegedly responsible.

The 15-year-old has been placed under judicial investigation under the supervision of the public prosecutor's office to establish the motives behind the incident. Police are still searching for a second minor suspected of involvement in the calls, which targeted several educational institutions in Casablanca.

ma.headline: Princess Lalla Oum Kalthoum oversees mental health agreement
ma.dek: A new partnership aims to boost mental health care in the Rabat-Salé-Kenitra region.
paragraphs: Princess Lalla Oumkeltoum visited the new 120-bed psychiatric hospital in Kenitra on Friday to enhance mental health services for the Rabat-Salé-Kenitra region. Her Royal Highness, president of the Lalla Oumkeltoum Foundation for Mental Health, toured various departments including the outpatient clinic, day hospital for the elderly, and addiction treatment unit. She learned about the operations and patient care at these facilities.

During the visit, Princess Lalla Oumkeltoum chaired a ceremony where a framework partnership agreement was signed between the Ministry of Health and Social Protection and the Lalla Oumkeltoum Foundation for Mental Health. This agreement supports the implementation of the national “Mental Health Plan 2030” and the Foundation’s own strategic action plan.

The Lalla Oumkeltoum Foundation is dedicated to promoting mental health for vulnerable individuals through awareness, prevention, and support initiatives. The partnership aims to assist people with mental disorders and their families, aligning with the foundation's statutes and the High Royal Care for mental well-being.

ug.headline: Uganda minister urges patience as DRC border stays shut
ug.dek: Dr Charles Ayume said border closure is vital to protect Ugandans from Ebola, despite calls for reopening.
paragraphs: Uganda's Minister for Primary Health Care, Dr Charles Ayume, asked for public patience as the country maintains its border closure with the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). The border was shut on May 27, 2026, due to an escalating Ebola outbreak in eastern DRC. Security forces have reinforced the border, but some Congolese nationals continue to enter Uganda through unofficial routes, seeking work, trade, or services. On November 6, 10 Congolese nationals were arrested inside Echuya National Park for illegal entry.

Ayume stated on Thursday at Katuna Border that the Ministry of Health's priority is safeguarding Ugandans from public health threats, not inconveniencing travellers. He warned that reopening the border while Ebola remains active in the DRC could trigger a new outbreak in Uganda and strain its health system. The minister also called for greater investment in thermal imaging cameras at major border crossings to detect suspected cases.

Uganda was declared Ebola-free in July after an outbreak that began in May and resulted in 20 confirmed cases and two deaths, with 15 linked to DRC imports. The DRC has reported over 10,600 confirmed cases and 5,100 deaths by November 3, according to the World Health Organisation (WHO). Uganda and Rwanda recently conducted joint cross-border health preparedness exercises to strengthen their response to public health emergencies.

ug.headline: EACOP outlines community investments as Uganda nears first oil
ug.dek: The East African Crude Oil Pipeline company says it is funding water, schools and health projects along the pipeline corridor, while it still struggles to restore land cleared.
paragraphs: The East African Crude Oil Pipeline (EACOP) says its work now centres on lasting community benefits and environmental responsibility as Uganda moves closer to first oil. Deputy Managing Director John Bosco Habumugisha made the case at the 4th Annual Joint Civil Society Conference organised by the Petroleum Authority of Uganda, held under the theme "Advancing Sustainability in Uganda's Oil and Gas Sector".

Habumugisha said the company is funding water solutions, solar energy for schools, support for girls' education and tree planting, alongside school Green Clubs. Among ongoing projects, a Health Centre II in Bunyoro is being upgraded to Health Centre III to improve maternal and child health services. EACOP is also training engineers with the China University of Petroleum, the Petroleum Authority of Uganda and Mbarara University.

EACOP Environmental Engineer Charity Tushemereirwe named the reinstatement of the pipeline right-of-way and wetlands among the project's most complex outstanding challenges. She said temporary access routes built during construction are now used by communities, which makes closing them difficult.

Groceries, fuel, dining, retail, hospitality, travel and online purchases are all covered. The campaign, called "Pay. Save. Get More.", is aimed mainly at existing cardholders who use their cards only occasionally.

ug.headline: Muhoozi promotes CID Director Magambo to Acting Lt Col
ug.dek: The promotion lifts Tom Magambo, who was appointed to lead the police's Criminal Investigations Directorate in 2022, into an army rank.
paragraphs: Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, the Chief of Defence Forces, has elevated Criminal Investigations Directorate (CID) Director AIGP Maj Tom Magambo to acting lieutenant colonel. Col Chris Magezi, acting director of Defence Public Information at the Ministry of Defence and Veteran Affairs, made the announcement.

Before leading CID, Magambo spent two decades at the Internal Security Organisation (ISO) from 2002, reaching chief intelligence officer and director of analysis. He later coordinated the Eastern Africa Fusion and Liaison Unit, which links Uganda with Ethiopia, Kenya, Sudan, South Sudan, Somalia, Tanzania, Djibouti, Burundi and Rwanda.

President Yoweri Museveni named him CID director on January 25, 2022, succeeding AIGP Grace Akullo, who had held the post for nearly a decade. Magambo had never been a police officer before that appointment, and Museveni regularised him as an AIGP in April 2022.

ug.headline: ADF stages first major attack on Uganda from Zaire
ug.dek: Around 600 fighters crossed from eastern Zaire at dawn and struck Kasese District, killing about 50 people in the first assault and driving an estimated 25,000 residents.
paragraphs: On November 13, 1996, about 600 heavily armed fighters from the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) crossed the Mpondwe-Lhubiriha river from Kasindi in eastern Zaire, now the Democratic Republic of the Congo, and attacked communities in Kasese District from around 6am. The rebels hit the Mpondwe Customs Post, Bwera township and nearby Karambi at the same time, overwhelming local defences in one of the most serious breaches of Uganda's western border at the time.

Around 50 people were reportedly killed in the first assault, and an estimated 25,000 residents abandoned the border corridor. Fighters carried off supplies, damaged infrastructure and seized civilians to serve as porters and recruits. They pulled back towards Zaire once Ugandan military reinforcements arrived.

The ADF had been formed in late 1995 by merging anti-government groups, including former members of the National Army for the Liberation of Uganda and radical Tabligh Islamist factions, and was led politically by Jamil Mukulu, a former Catholic turned Tabligh cleric. Within days the Uganda People's Defence Force crossed into Zaire, took the border town of Kasindi and attacked ADF rear camps.

zw.headline: Delta Corporation lifts half-year operating income 13% to US$112.2 million
zw.dek: Zimbabwe's largest beverage maker says domestic lager, sorghum beer and spirits volumes drove the gain, while a US$97 million tax claim hangs over the group.
paragraphs: Delta Corporation, Zimbabwe's largest beverage company, has posted operating income of US$112.2 million for the half year, up 13% from US$99.6 million a year earlier. Group revenue rose 18% to US$607.5 million over the six months to September 30.

Volume growth came from domestic lager, sorghum beer and spirits, with lager up 13% to 1.75 million hectolitres and Chibuku Super sales rising 27%. The company credited relative exchange rate stability, mining activity, diaspora remittances and liquidity from the agricultural marketing season, and said 97% of its revenue now comes from domestic foreign currency sales. The board declared an interim dividend of US$2.40 per share, a 20% increase.

Delta is contesting a US$97 million tax assessment from the Zimbabwe Revenue Authority covering 2019 to 2024, which the company says would have a material impact if upheld. It named economic policy stability and a review of the sugar tax as its priorities for the year.

The two had challenged resolutions from an October 20 extraordinary general meeting that approved their dismissal and appointed Munyaradzi Nzarayapenga as interim board chairman.

cv.headline: Neves seeks second term in Cape Verde election
cv.dek: Incumbent President José Maria Neves faces six challengers in an election testing the nation's democratic stability.
paragraphs: Cape Verdeans vote on Sunday for their president, with incumbent José Maria Neves expected to win a second term. Six candidates are competing, including former justice minister Joana Rosa Amado, who aims to be the country's first female president. The election is seen as a measure of democratic stability in the Portuguese-speaking island nation.

The election occurs as Cape Verde's national football team made a historic debut at the World Cup, reaching the knockout stages. Tourism, which contributes about a quarter of the economy, is also experiencing a boom. However, the country faces challenges such as rising living costs, youth unemployment, and social inequality.

Cape Verde's economy is significantly supported by its diaspora, whose population abroad is estimated to be nearly three times the number of residents. Voters will decide if the nation can maintain its democratic reputation while addressing economic and social pressures.

cv.headline: Cape Verde state reform needed to boost wealth creation
cv.dek: A political analysis argues the nation's state structure is designed for scarcity, not wealth production.
paragraphs: Cape Verde's state structure is showing signs of exhaustion, designed to manage scarcity and protect a vulnerable society rather than organize wealth production and economic autonomy. This original sin of state-building transformed a historical need for protection into a lasting culture of dependency, according to a political analysis.

The roots of this problem predate independence in 1975, stemming from the archipelago's integration into Atlantic circuits serving external interests, marked by slave trading, intermediation economies, and agricultural fragility. Emigration became a common response to a lack of economic horizons, with citizens' resistance lacking conditions for productive conversion.

While independence brought sovereignty and democracy consolidated freedoms, a productive transformation has not matched political gains. The nation remains heavily reliant on imports, tourism, remittances, and external flows, lacking a diversified industrial base. The analysis calls for intelligent industrial policy focused on agro-food processing, fisheries, naval repair, water and energy industries, and exportable technologies and services.

cv.headline: Cape Verdean Dino d’Santiago wins Latin Grammy with Brazilian artists
cv.dek: The award went to the album "Criolo, Amaro & Dino", recorded with Brazilian rapper Criolo and pianist Amaro Freitas from Recife.
paragraphs: Cape Verdean musician Dino d’Santiago won a Latin Grammy on Friday, 12 November, in Las Vegas, United States. The prize was in the category of Best Brazilian Popular Music/Afro-Portuguese Brazilian Music Album for "Criolo, Amaro & Dino", which he recorded with Brazilian artists Criolo and Amaro Freitas.

Accepting the award, d’Santiago named Cape Verde, Angola, Mozambique, Guinea-Bissau, São Tomé and Príncipe and Portugal, and thanked the Portuguese language for making them one people. Freitas, born in Recife, said the work joins Black music and the African diaspora across the world, while Criolo dedicated the win to Indigenous peoples in Brazil.

The album has 12 tracks mixing rap, Brazilian popular music, jazz, morna and funaná. The three artists split studio sessions between Rio de Janeiro, Recife, São Paulo and Lisbon. The project began with the song "Esperança", released in 2024, which earned d’Santiago his first Latin Grammy nomination that year.

td.headline: Chad students end university strike
td.dek: The National Union of Chadian Students (UNET) lifted a three-day strike at the University of N'Djamena on November 13, 2026, but maintained its demands.
paragraphs: The National Union of Chadian Students (UNET) at the University of N'Djamena announced on November 13, 2026, that it had ended a strike that began three days earlier. The student organization cited actions taken by the National Centre for University Services (CNOU) as the reason for lifting the strike, while affirming that their demands remain unresolved.

After three days of protests, UNET has called for students to resume their university activities. In a statement, the organization thanked the striking students for their mobilization and sense of responsibility. It urged everyone to return to classes calmly and with respect.

UNET also issued a call for unity and responsibility, encouraging students to continue working towards improving their living and study conditions. This objective remains a priority for the organization despite the lifting of the strike.

td.headline: Sarh students gain seven buses for campus travel
td.dek: The government supplied three new and four used buses to the university's student services centre, and students report mixed views on their condition.
paragraphs: Seven buses, three new and four used, have been in service for a month for students at the University of Sarh in southern Chad, moving them between their homes and the university sites. The vehicles were supplied by the government to the Centre secondaire des œuvres universitaires (CSOU), the body that runs student services at the university.

Many students say the buses bring relief from transport problems they faced regularly, though some have doubts about the state and comfort of the used vehicles. Tambarina Mitterand, secretary general of the Union nationale des étudiants tchadiens (UNET) in the Moyen-Chari region, said the buses answer a problem that weighed heavily on student travel, and he urged students to look after them.

Nanlangar Kodalbaye, director of the CSOU in Sarh, thanked the government and said steps will be taken to manage the buses better and end overcrowding. He also said measures are being considered to improve university meals, including hygiene, meal quality and portion sizes.

td.headline: N'Djamena street food risks health
td.dek: Uncovered food sold in Chad's capital is exposed to dust, flies, and exhaust fumes, raising health concerns.
paragraphs: In N'Djamena, Chad, food items like potatoes, locusts, grilled sweet potatoes, and watermelon slices are sold openly in markets and streets, often near busy roads. These foods are exposed to dust, flies, and exhaust fumes, creating significant health worries for consumers despite enabling small traders to earn a living.

Residents express alarm over the unsanitary conditions, with one N'Djamena inhabitant noting that customers continue to buy food with flies landing directly on it. Vendors cite difficulties such as a lack of appropriate selling spaces and the challenge of completely avoiding contamination from flies and dust.

Health experts warn that unprotected food can carry pathogens that cause foodborne illnesses like acute diarrhea or poisoning. The visible sale of exposed food items across the city's streets and sidewalks highlights a critical public health issue.

td.headline: Chad hosts Africa Executive Meeting to boost trade
td.dek: N'Djamena meeting focuses on transport corridors, youth employment, and investment to foster African economic integration.
paragraphs: The Africa Executive Meeting 2026 convened in N'Djamena on Friday, November 13, focusing on transport corridors, inter-African trade, youth employment, and investment. The gathering aimed to convert cooperation possibilities into projects that create value and jobs.

Institutional representatives and economic actors discussed themes including "corridors, decongestion, and inter-African trade," "human capital, youth employment, and entrepreneurship," and "industrial transformation and investment." Abderrahmane Gademi, interim administrator of Chad's Chamber of Commerce, Industry, Agriculture, Mines, and Crafts, expressed a desire to support and encourage participation in the event.

Discussions highlighted the need for economic actors' participation, financing mobilization, and infrastructure for better goods circulation. The meeting was intended as a platform for exchanges and for forging partnerships to develop new market prospects.

td.headline: Dakhla seeks stronger Chad economic ties
td.dek: Morocco's Dakhla-Oued Eddahab region wants to boost trade with Chad in farming, training, tourism, and renewables.
paragraphs: El Khattat Yanja, president of the Dakhla-Oued Eddahab Regional Council, wants to increase economic exchanges with Chad. He expressed this desire during a visit to N'Djamena for the Africa Executive Meetings on Friday, November 13. Yanja highlighted his region's development strategy, focusing on fishing, agriculture, tourism, renewable energy, and port infrastructure.

The Dakhla-Oued Eddahab region, in southern Morocco, is being positioned as a key economic hub for sub-Saharan Africa. Yanja presented the development levers of this region, emphasizing investments made since 2015 under a new development model for southern regions. Efforts to improve air connectivity and attract investors were also noted.
The Moroccan official aims to foster cooperation in agriculture, training, tourism, and renewable energies. These sectors form the core of the region's strategy to become a logistical pole.

dj.headline: Djibouti parliament approves cancer centre loan
dj.dek: Djibouti's parliament has adopted nine legislative texts, including a loan for a new cancer treatment centre.
paragraphs: Djibouti's parliament convened for its second ordinary session, with President Dileita Mohamed Dileita opening the plenary meeting attended by Prime Minister Abdoulkader Kamil Mohamed and government ministers. Lawmakers welcomed the new Minister of Defence, Aden Ali Mahamade, who was present for the first time since his appointment. The assembly's agenda included a reform of the associations' regime, the ratification of a loan agreement with the Islamic Development Bank (IDB), and the amended finance law for 2026.

The parliament also approved the financial statements for seven public institutions, covering 2024 for the ADR, SIAF, and Electricité de Djibouti (EDD), and 2025 for ADDS, AID, ARULOS, and the Diwan of Wakf Properties. Deputies questioned the executive on the new framework for associations and the conditions of the IDB financing. Ministers responded to all inquiries regarding these matters and the management of public entities' accounts.

Prime Minister Abdoulkader Kamil Mohamed highlighted the future oncology centre, intended to improve early cancer detection and treatment locally, thereby reducing costly overseas medical evacuations. He acknowledged the crucial role of the National Social Security Fund (CNSS) as a partner in this health initiative. Discussions also covered energy production, hydrocarbons, and renewable energy development, with an update on the improved financial standing of SIAF and Electricité de Djibouti.

dj.headline: Djibouti puts its connectivity figures before the ITU in Qatar
dj.dek: Around 70% of the population now uses the internet, and 350 kilometres of fibre are being laid towards the north of the country.
paragraphs: At the plenipotentiary conference of the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), held in the Qatari capital, Djibouti's Minister of Communication, in charge of Posts and Telecommunications, Mohamed Abdoulkader Moussa, told delegates that developing countries should be full actors in designing new technologies, not simply users of them.

He said telecommunications have become a strategic lever for development and independence for states. The minister linked the sector to the national Vision 2035 led by President Ismaïl Omar Guelleh, and recalled that the National Assembly adopted a digital code in June 2025 covering electronic communications, personal data protection, cybersecurity, e-commerce, online administration and consumer rights.

The minister acknowledged that closing gaps between regions and reaching the most remote areas remains a challenge. Djibouti has also adopted a national emergency telecommunications plan (NETP) to keep communications running during crises, with satellite technology presented as a complement for isolated areas.

dj.headline: Djibouti and Qatar discuss data centre cooperation in Doha
dj.dek: Djibouti's communications minister, Helem, held talks with his Qatari counterpart, Al Mannai, on the sidelines of an ITU conference.
paragraphs: Djibouti's minister Helem met Qatari minister Al Mannai in Doha, the Qatari capital, while attending the Plenipotentiary Conference of the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), the United Nations agency for digital technologies, which opened on Monday. The two sides reviewed the state of their cooperation on three topics: capacity building, communications and the development of data centres.

Helem praised the quality of the cooperation between the two countries and reaffirmed Djibouti's commitment to consolidating the partnership. Al Mannai praised the close and productive ties and said the Qatari government was determined to strengthen the cooperation further. Djibouti's ambassador to Qatar, Dayib Doubad Robleh, attended the meeting.

The ITU conference takes place every four years and is the union's supreme decision-making body, bringing together representatives of its 194 member states at the exhibition and congress centre in Doha. Delegates are due to elect the organisation's leadership for the next four years.

sz.headline: NGO criticised for advertising unpaid skilled roles in Eswatini
sz.dek: Eswatini's coordinating body for NGOs has warned against exploiting unemployed graduates through unpaid positions.
paragraphs: An NGO in Eswatini has come under fire for advertising unpaid volunteer positions that require specialised medical qualifications and professional skills. The advertisement offered roles in critical care, emergency care, medical data and research, and has raised questions about whether NGOs are taking advantage of unemployed graduates.

The Coordinating Assembly of Non-Governmental Organisations (CANGO), an umbrella body for more than 70 NGOs, has warned against exploiting graduates through unpaid positions. Its executive director, Thembinkosi Dlamini, said organisations often cite a lack of funding for unpaid roles, but he expressed concern that some volunteers were expected to work beyond agreed hours and duties without clear pay arrangements.

Dlamini said genuine volunteer programmes should have clear agreements that define responsibilities and separate volunteer roles from those of permanent employees. He said CANGO opposes exploitation in the workplace, and that the Employment Act and Industrial Relations Act mainly cover formal employer-employee relationships.

sz.headline: Taiwan partners Eswatini on diabetes prevention
sz.dek: A World Diabetes Day campaign at Siphocosini Constituency Centre focused on early action and preventive measures.
paragraphs: Taiwan and Eswatini's Ministry of Health partnered for a World Diabetes Day campaign at Siphocosini Constituency Centre, focusing on diabetes prevention and early detection. Taiwan's Ambassador to Eswatini, Ching-Lin Tsuei, stated his country supports Eswatini in managing non-communicable diseases, emphasizing proactive health measures.

Minister of Health Mduduzi Matsebula highlighted the dangers of poorly managed diabetes and urged residents to adopt healthier routines, including increased physical activity and reduced alcohol consumption. He also stressed the importance of regular medical check-ups for early identification of complications.
The campaign, held under the 2026 World Diabetes Day theme 'Early action on diabetes,' provided residents with health services and information. World Diabetes Day is observed annually on November 14.

sz.headline: Eswatini seeks UK help on border security
sz.dek: Minister Shakantu met with UK Minister Turley to discuss managing migration and asylum seekers.
paragraphs: Eswatini's Minister for Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, Senator Pholile Shakantu, met with United Kingdom Minister of State for Border Security and Asylum, The Rt Hon Anna Turley MP, in Mbabane to discuss strengthening border security and asylum processes. The Kingdom of Eswatini is experiencing an increase in refugees and asylum seekers and seeks to manage the situation proactively.

The two ministers explored cooperation in managing migration fairly, orderly, and securely, including sharing experiences, improving asylum processes, combating human trafficking, and enhancing information sharing. Eswatini aims to strengthen its laws, policies, systems, and controls to safeguard national security and uphold human dignity while meeting international obligations.

Senator Shakantu also observed proceedings in the UK Parliament during her visit. The discussions highlighted Eswatini's commitment to its friendship with the United Kingdom and its desire to deepen cooperation on these critical issues.

sz.headline: Eswatini hands regional trade leadership to Namibia
sz.dek: Mluleki Dlamini, Eswatini's Director of MSMEs, outlined past initiatives and regional trade challenges at a Windhoek meeting.
paragraphs: Eswatini has transferred its leadership of the Southern African Bureau of the Intergovernmental Committee of Senior Officials and Experts (ICSOE) to Namibia. The handover occurred during a high-level economic meeting in Windhoek from November 10 to 13, 2026, organised by the Government of Namibia and the United Nations Economic Commission for Africa (UNECA).

Mluleki Dlamini, Eswatini's Director of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) and outgoing Chairperson of the Southern African Bureau, presented initiatives from Eswatini's tenure. These included support for Angola's African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) strategy, MSME development in Eswatini, and capacity-building for small businesses in Lesotho. Dlamini also highlighted trade barriers such as differing regulations, documentation, inadequate transport investment, and insufficient digital infrastructure.

The meeting aimed to strengthen regional trade and economic integration, with discussions focusing on persistent obstacles affecting cross-border trade. Dlamini called for harmonised regulations among regional economic communities to facilitate the smooth movement of goods and services as African countries implement the AfCFTA.

sz.headline: Mbabane equips 48 youths with business, crochet skills
sz.dek: The Municipal Council of Mbabane partnered with two organisations to train young people in entrepreneurship and crocheting.
paragraphs: Graduates from a Mbabane programme now hold business and craft certificates: 48 young people completed training backed by the Municipal Council of Mbabane (MCM). Of them, 23 took entrepreneurship courses run with Kwakha Indvodza, covering tax compliance, financial management and other business basics over one week. 25 more learned crocheting through Crafty Hook, a local crochet business.

At the graduation, Mayor Thulani Mkhonto, city councillors and MCM Chief Executive Officer Gciniwe Fakudze presented the certificates. Fakudze told the graduates the training should be a starting point, and urged young women in particular to earn extra income with their hands. Mkhonto said a skill cannot be taken away from its holder, and urged graduates to use theirs to improve their livelihoods.

Buyiswa Nkambule, one of the entrepreneurship graduates, thanked Kwakha Indvodza and the council for the training. A separate Eswatini Positive News report says Ntombikayise Dlamini received a certificate for The Cozy Crochet Experience on 13 November 2026, and that Sisekelo Dlamini was the only male on that five-week course.

ga.headline: Gabon's new anti-smoking law expands controls, but enforcement doubts persist
ga.dek: The law, promulgated in September 2026, now covers nicotine-derived products such as e-cigarettes and bans retail sales of cigarettes.
paragraphs: Gabon promulgated a new anti-smoking law in September 2026 that extends its reach to nicotine-derived products, including e-cigarettes. It also bans retail sales of cigarettes and requires a specific licence to sell tobacco.

Georgy Silver Anthony Mba Nkogo, president of the NGO SOS Tabagisme Gabon, welcomed the measures, which his organisation has campaigned for for nearly 10 years. He fears they will meet the same fate as the 2013 law, which had no operational mechanism for control. He said only the advertising ban is partially respected, while health warnings, public smoking bans and the ban on sales to minors are still widely flouted.
Mba Nkogo also pointed to the missing national commission against smoking, provided for in the 2013 law, which he says is needed to coordinate action, monitor measures and enforce them on the ground.

ga.headline: Gabon maps 319 unfinished Libreville buildings and their owners
ga.dek: The government is now working out the legal status of each site before deciding what to do with its owner.
paragraphs: The Gabonese government has counted 319 unfinished buildings across the Greater Libreville area, following instructions from President Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema on August 16, 2026. Vice-President Hermann Immongault chaired a working session on November 12, 2026, with the ministers for housing and public works to review the survey.

The inventory was carried out by the housing ministry's departments. Officials are now establishing the legal position of each property to decide the responsibilities of its owners. Minister Millot Lambert Mouvinde said the work covers buildings, bare plots and risk zones along several main roads.

A file has been compiled for most of the surveyed buildings, recording their location, the owners' identities, the use of each site and its GPS coordinates. Immongault asked for the two ministries' reports to be merged into one summary with a detailed timetable, due within two weeks. The president had warned that the state could requisition sites in the public interest, after owners are formally notified.

ga.headline: Gabon seeks fairer EU raw materials partnership
ga.dek: Gabon's National Assembly president called for local processing, technology transfer, and job creation in producer countries.
paragraphs: Gabon's National Assembly president, Michel Régis Onanga Ndiaye, called for a more equitable economic partnership with the European Union during the second EU-ACP Parliamentary Assembly in Brussels. He advocated for increased local transformation of raw materials, technology transfers, and job creation in producer nations, emphasizing industrial sovereignty in cooperation.

Ambassador Régis Immongault stated that access to strategic raw materials should not be the sole objective of the EU-ACP partnership. The Gabonese delegation, also including Senate First Vice-President Serge Maurice Mabiala, pushed for a better distribution of economic benefits from natural resource exploitation. Gabon wants productive investments, technology, local industries, and skilled jobs, not just raw material supply.

This demand aligns with Gabon's economic diversification goals, aiming to move beyond exporting unprocessed raw materials, as shown by the planned ban on raw manganese exports from January 1, 2029. Gabon also seeks participation in the future Africa-EU Parliamentary Working Group on critical raw materials to defend producers' interests in resource governance.

ga.headline: Gabon invites Erdoğan to Libreville to deepen Turkey ties
ga.dek: Vice President Alexandre Barro Chambrier handed the invitation to Turkish Vice President Cevdet Yilmaz at the COP31 leaders' summit in Antalya.
paragraphs: Gabon's President Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema has invited Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan to visit Libreville, a move meant to consolidate relations between the two countries and open new investment prospects. Vice President Alexandre Barro Chambrier delivered the invitation to his Turkish counterpart on the sidelines of the summit.

The move follows Oligui Nguema's state visit to Turkey from July 30 to August 2, 2025, which produced eight cooperation agreements. Turkey's Summa Construction is building the presidential villas, a zoo and the Centre des congrès in Libreville's Cité de la démocratie, which was 45% complete in June 2025. Karpowership, part of Karadeniz Energy, supplies up to 150 MW to the national utility SEEG under a five-year contract.

Turkish exports to Gabon rose from about $13 million in 2008 to $126.5 million in 2025, according to the Turkish embassy in Libreville, which published the figures in May 2026. Total bilateral trade exceeded $160 million. The last Turkish president to visit Gabon was Abdullah Gül, in March 2011.

ga.headline: Gabon seeks a voice at Francophonie summit in Cambodia
ga.dek: Foreign Minister Marie-Édith Tassyla-Ye-Doumbeneny leads Gabon's delegation to the 20th Francophonie Summit, which gathers 90 member states.
paragraphs: Foreign Minister Marie-Édith Tassyla-Ye-Doumbeneny is representing President Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema at the 20th Francophonie Summit in Phnom Penh, Cambodia, on November 15 and 16, 2026. Libreville wants to shape debates on the future of the organisation, including peace, cooperation and shared prosperity. On arrival she was welcomed by Long Yes, under-secretary of state at the Cambodian foreign ministry.

The minister's ministry said the summit is not just another meeting, and that Gabon wants to help decide the direction of the French-speaking space. Before the sessions, she held a working meeting with her delegation, including Alfred Nguia Banda, Gabon's ambassador to France. The summit, themed "Reinvesting in peace for shared prosperity and lasting stability", brings together representatives of 90 member states and governments.

The talks will cover political, economic, cultural and educational cooperation, and the role of the Francophonie in multilateral diplomacy and crisis prevention. The next secretary general of the Organisation internationale de la Francophonie (OIF) is also due to be elected at the summit.

gm.headline: Gambia's parties sign peace accord ahead of December election
gm.dek: Parties, the electoral commission and international bodies pledged to keep the December 5 presidential vote free of violence and intimidation.
paragraphs: Political parties and national and international stakeholders signed a revised peace accord on Thursday, November 12, at the International Conference Centre, ahead of The Gambia's December 5 presidential election. The 2026 Janjanbureh Peace Accord aims to prevent electoral violence, intimidation, hate speech and political intolerance.

The Inter-Party Committee (IPC) brought together registered parties, the Independent Electoral Commission, the United Nations, the African Union, ECOWAS, the European Union, civil society and religious communities. IPC Co-Chair Ejatou Jallow said political competition should never lead to violence or hatred, and called on women, young people and marginalised groups to take part without fear.

UNDP Resident Coordinator Mandisa Mashologu said the accord's success would depend on party leaders and their supporters. The European Union said it would deploy an independent Election Observation Mission at the government's invitation, and ECOWAS urged parties to share the commitments with candidates, polling agents and supporters across the country.

gm.headline: Darbo files presidential papers as independent, backed by coalition
gm.dek: Independent candidate Lamin J. Darbo handed in his documents to the electoral commission on Wednesday, with the Team Gambia Grand Coalition behind him.
paragraphs: Lamin J. Darbo lodged his nomination papers for the December 5 presidential election at the Independent Electoral Commission's Election House in Kanifing on Wednesday, November 11. He presents himself as an independent candidate, and the Team Gambia Grand Coalition is backing him, with its coordinators and veteran politicians Halifa Sallah and Sidia Jatta at his side.

IEC chairperson Joseph Colley said Darbo had supplied documents covering citizenship, age, education, voter registration, nominators and the nomination deposit, among other items. Colley said the Commission would carry out its due diligence before issuing a final decision. Darbo said he was no longer representing the National Unity Party, and Colley confirmed receipt of his resignation letter.

Colley issued Darbo a nomination receipt and a copy of the documents and campaign code. Endorsed candidates are to meet on November 15 to plan their campaign schedules and sign a peace pact on November 16. The Commission will publish its list of withdrawn, accepted and rejected candidates at 6 pm on November 14.

gm.dek: GACH Global Trading Company Limited is suing two former officials over funds allegedly obtained through a fraudulent petroleum supply deal.
paragraphs: Essa Faal, a prominent Gambian lawyer and politician, came up on Wednesday during a civil fraud case over a D58.9 million dispute at the High Court in Banjul. During cross-examination, plaintiff's counsel Ida Drameh asked second defendant Saihou Drammeh whether he knew Faal, and he said he did. Drameh then put it to him that Faal had subsequently owed money, which Drammeh acknowledged before Justice Ebrima Jaiteh.

Drammeh rejected the claim that he had said Faal used the money on politics, answering "No, My Lord" when asked whether he had made that statement. Earlier in the hearing, Drameh had suggested Drammeh complained that Kebba Ceesay registered two apartments valued at €48,000 in his own name, an allegation Drammeh also rejected.

The suit, GACH Global Trading Company Limited against Kaddijatou Kebbeh and Saihou Drammeh, was filed in January 2022. The company seeks over D58.9 million and $221,000 tied to a September 2021 petroleum product agreement, plus interest of 24% and 4% until payment.

gm.headline: Gambia hosts regional maritime ministers in Banjul
gm.dek: Ministers and experts from West and Central Africa will weigh a proposed regional maritime bank and the transformation of MOWCA into a continental body.
paragraphs: The Ministry of Transport, Works and Infrastructure will host the 12th Ordinary Session of the Bureau of Ministers of the Maritime Organization of West and Central Africa (MOWCA) on 16 and 17 November 2026 in Banjul. Ministers, senior government officials and maritime experts from across the region will attend.

Discussions will cover the implementation of MOWCA's 2026 work programme, the proposed Regional Maritime Development Bank, institutional and financial reforms, and member states' contributions under the Regional Maritime Fund. Delegates will also consider the proposed transformation of MOWCA into the African Maritime Organization and a proposal to convene the first MOWCA Summit of Heads of State. Counsel Olimatou Danso-Malang, Director General of the Gambia Maritime Administration, said regional commitments must be turned into concrete action on maritime safety, security, port development and the blue economy.

Recommendations from the technical Meeting of Experts will be consolidated into draft recommendations for the Bureau of Ministers to consider. Earlier this year, Minister Ebrima Sillah assumed the MOWCA Chairmanship, and Danso-Malang was elected Chairperson of the Committee of Experts.

gm.headline: Gambian women left behind after fighting for democracy
gm.dek: Women who led the 'Kalama Revolution' against dictator Jammeh now find themselves excluded from power-sharing.
paragraphs: Adama Bah, a politician and traditional singer from Sukuta, recalls the "Kalama Revolution" in April 2016 when women carried calabashes and brooms to the courthouse. This protest movement emerged from frustration with dictator Yahya Jammeh's regime, leading to the arrest of Ousainu Darboe and dozens of United Democratic Party (UDP) members. Bah stated that fear left the city as women stormed Banjul, contributing to Jammeh's eventual defeat.

A decade after their sacrifices, women who were at the forefront of the struggle for democracy in Gambia have been systematically excluded from power. Bah, who joined the UDP in 1996, noted that many of her colleagues from the "Kalama Revolution" are now deceased or too old, their bodies broken by state-sponsored abuse. Iconic figures like Nogoi Njie and Sukai Dahaba have passed away, leaving a legacy of betrayal where women are used for political gain but discarded during power distribution.

Bah explained that politicians establish parties with women in mind, but it is the women who endure hardship, leaving their homes and children to support politicians in remote areas. She believes a lack of formal education is a significant barrier, preventing women like herself from holding positions. She stated, "Personally, I don’t have a position because I am not educated. If I was, I would be given a position."

gn.headline: Guinea's gold mining ban drives thousands from Siguiri mining sites
gn.dek: Miners and their families are leaving Kintinian and nearby gold areas after the government banned unregulated artisanal gold digging, a measure announced on 2 November.
paragraphs: Thousands of artisanal gold miners and their families are leaving the mining areas of Siguiri, in northern Guinea, after the government banned unregulated artisanal gold mining in the region. Departures are multiplying in the new prefecture of Kintinian, including Bouré Nafadji, as workers lose their main source of income.

Mohamed Camara, originally from Kissidougou, said he is heading home because he depends entirely on gold digging and has no other trade. Nafina Traoré, a native of Faranah, said her family has no money left and her children sometimes go a full day without eating, and she has appealed to President Mamadi Doumbouya to help women.

Abou Touré is leaving Kintinian before his savings run out rather than wait for the support measures the authorities have announced. The government says the ban is meant to stop soil degradation, the destruction of farmland and the pollution of waterways caused by the activity.

gn.headline: Doumbouya signs Guinea's 2026 revised budget law
gn.dek: President Mamadi Doumbouya has enacted the revised finance law and allocated funds to ministries.
paragraphs: President Mamadi Doumbouya of Guinea has officially enacted the Revised Finance Law (LFR) for 2026, following its approval by the Parliament. The decree, announced on Friday, November 13, 2026, formalizes the ordinary law L/2026/005/AN, dated November 7, 2026, which pertains to the current fiscal year's finances.

In a subsequent official act on the same day, President Doumbouya issued a decree to distribute the payment credits from the state budget among various ministerial departments and republican institutions for 2026. These decrees become effective immediately upon their signing and will be officially registered and published in the Republic's Official Journal.
The revised budget law and the decree on credit allocation are now in effect, guiding the financial operations of Guinea's government ministries and institutions for the remainder of 2026.

gn.headline: Guinea's election chief warned of pressure
gn.dek: Minister Djenabou Touré urged Mohamed Aly Condé to prioritize Guinea's interests over political or personal demands.
paragraphs: Djenabou Touré, Guinea's Minister of Territorial Administration and Decentralization, officially installed Mohamed Aly Condé as the new Director General of Elections on Friday, November 13, 2026. Condé faces the significant task of organizing upcoming senatorial and regional elections by the end of the year, as well as supplementary elections in 2027.

Minister Touré cautioned Condé about the intense daily pressures he will encounter from candidates, authorities, and the public, often fueled by misinformation. She stressed the importance of adhering strictly to the law and regulations, advising him to listen to all advice but ultimately do what is right and good for Guinea, not for individual candidates or herself.

Touré also emphasized the need for close collaboration with the Deputy Director General and other stakeholders, including the press and civil society, to ensure professional and impartial electoral operations. Condé, formerly a legal advisor to the institution, pledged to uphold impartiality and continue the work to consolidate Guinea's institutional framework.

gn.headline: Brooklyn building collapse kills two Guineans, injures pregnant survivor
gn.dek: Search operations continue at the Flatbush site, where eight people died when a three-storey building fell on Wednesday, 11 November.
paragraphs: A three-storey building collapsed in Brooklyn's Flatbush neighbourhood, New York, on Wednesday, 11 November 2026, killing eight people, including two Guinean nationals. About 10 others were injured, among them a Guinean woman, Fatoumata Binta Bah, who was pulled from the rubble with her baby.

Her husband, Mamadou Mouctar Baldé, a Guinean who shared the apartment with the victims, said he had left the building only five minutes before it fell. The two men who died, Mamadou Bhoye Barry and Mamadou Bhoye Ndiaye, were both from Guinea-Conakry. Baldé said Ndiaye had been lying down until a courier arrived with an online order for him.

The Guinean Community of America (GUICA NY), which represents the diaspora in New York, said condolences will be received on 15 November from 18:30 at the Utica Mosque, 65 Utica Avenue, Brooklyn. Rescue operations were still under way at the site, and the group said it would share reliable updates as they become available.

gn.headline: BCA SARL attends Simandou Mining Summit
gn.dek: The Guinean industrial supplier showcased its global network of 250 suppliers at the Conakry event.
paragraphs: BCA SARL, a Guinean industrial supply company, participated in the Simandou Mining Summit 2026 in Conakry from November 11 to 14. The company, represented by its General Manager M. Éloi César TOLNO, highlighted its role as a structured and reliable partner for Guinea's private sector. BCA SARL has over five years of experience and a global network of 250 professional suppliers.

The summit, themed 'Mining industry, engine of economic diversification in the era of Simandou 2040,' aimed to foster business between international investors, mining operators, financial institutions, and Guinean private sector actors. BCA SARL positioned itself as a qualified player in the industrial value chain, capable of meeting the new supply demands generated by the Simandou 2040 national industrialization roadmap, which represents over 200 billion USD in investments over 15 years.

BCA SARL specializes in supplying technical supplies, construction equipment, specialized consumables, and professional tools to sectors including mining, oil and gas, construction, energy, and public administration. The company's strength lies in its rigorously qualified global supplier network, ensuring clients find necessary products at the best prices, delivery times, and compliance standards without leaving Guinea.

gw.headline: Guinea-Bissau official flags shortages of staff, equipment and medicines
gw.dek: Fodé Caramba Sanhá urged citizens, schools and religious groups to share the work of preventing diabetes.
paragraphs: Fodé Caramba Sanhá, the first vice-president of Guinea-Bissau's National Transition Council (CNT), warned on Friday, November 13, 2026, that the country's health system lacks staff, equipment and medicines, and that many people struggle to reach care.

He made the remarks at the opening of a technical debate on diabetes prevention and control, held at the National People's Assembly ahead of World Diabetes Day on November 14. He called diabetes one of the main public health challenges in the country and said the response needs the state, health workers, families, schools, civil society and religious bodies. "Each citizen must take responsibility for their own health," he said.

Sanhá called for stronger awareness campaigns, healthy eating, regular physical activity, screening and ongoing follow-up for people living with diabetes. He said efforts should focus on vulnerable groups and remote communities far from main health centres.

gw.headline: Frente Popular asks new prosecutor to investigate activist's killing
gw.dek: The party wants a fast, independent probe into the murder of Vigário Luís Balanta and an end to military restrictions it calls unconstitutional.
paragraphs: Mário Yala, the newly appointed Attorney General, has been urged by the Frente Popular to ensure a swift, rigorous and impartial inquiry into the killing of the activist Vigário Luís Balanta, so that the facts come out and both the material and moral authors of the crime are held to account.

In a statement dated 13 November 2026, seen by the newspaper O Democrata, the party called for measures against delays, inaction and favouritism in the prosecution service. It also asked authorities to give the public regular updates on how the cases are progressing, within the limits of judicial secrecy.

gw.headline: Guinea-Bissau draws with Madagascar, keeps Group L lead
gw.dek: The national football team drew one-all with Madagascar in Morocco, maintaining their top position in CAN 2027 qualifying.
paragraphs: Guinea-Bissau drew one-all with Madagascar on Thursday, November 12, 2026, in their third match of the African Cup of Nations (CAN 2027) qualification Group L. The result means the Djurtus, who had won their previous two matches, maintain their lead in the group with seven points.

The match, played in Morocco where Madagascar hosts its home games, saw Guinea-Bissau's coach Emiliano Té make several changes to the starting lineup with less-used players. Despite controlling possession for much of the game, the team struggled to create clear scoring chances. Madagascar's Warren Caddy opened the scoring in the 59th minute, with Guinea-Bissau's goalkeeper Fernando Embadje making crucial saves throughout the encounter.

This draw prevents Guinea-Bissau from extending their lead over Nigeria, a strong contender for qualification. The team's performance in the first half was described as poor, with both sides showing difficulties in offensive build-up and frequent loss of possession. The next matchday will determine if they can solidify their position at the top of the group.

lr.headline: China opens zero-tariff market to Liberia and 52 African countries
lr.dek: Eligible products from the 53 African nations that maintain diplomatic relations with Beijing can now enter China without import duties.
paragraphs: China has announced a zero-tariff policy covering Liberia and 52 other African countries, allowing eligible products to enter the Chinese market without applicable import duties. Chinese Ambassador to Liberia Yin Chengwu disclosed the policy at a media briefing at the Chinese Embassy in Monrovia on Wednesday, November 11. He said China has extended zero-tariff treatment to 63 countries in total, including 53 African nations that maintain diplomatic relations with Beijing.

The embassy pointed to two major Chinese trade fairs, the China International Import Expo (CIIE) and the Canton Fair, as places where African businesses can meet Chinese buyers. It said the ninth CIIE drew more than 4,100 overseas enterprises from 162 countries, regions and international organisations, and that free exhibition space for least developed countries rose by 17 percent. A matchmaking event for Asian and African food and agricultural products was also held to connect exporters with buyers.

The embassy encouraged Liberian businesses to use the zero-tariff arrangement and take part in international trade exhibitions. China remains a major trading partner of Liberia, with cooperation covering infrastructure, trade, healthcare and development assistance. Vice President Jeremiah Kpan Koung recently led a Liberian delegation to China for the opening of the ninth CIIE.

It said the ninth CIIE drew more than 4,100 overseas enterprises from 162 countries, regions and international organisations, and that free exhibition space for least developed countries rose by 17 percent. China remains a major trading partner of Liberia, with cooperation covering infrastructure, trade, healthcare and development assistance. Vice President Jeremiah Kpan Koung recently led a Liberian delegation to China for the opening of the ninth CIIE.

lr.headline: Liberia's climate finance gap delays projects
lr.dek: While US$213 million of US$573 million identified funding was disbursed by December 2024, key climate projects remain unfinished.
paragraphs: African leaders at the United Nations climate conference in Türkiye called for predictable climate finance, but Liberia faces a significant funding gap for its climate plan. The country had identified about US$573 million in financing needs, but only US$213 million had been disbursed by December 2024, leaving approximately US$360 million outstanding.

Key projects aimed at improving weather forecasting and protecting Monrovia from coastal erosion are delayed due to this funding shortfall. Experts argue that adaptation needs grants rather than loans, as debt repayments limit resources for public services. Questions remain over whether climate finance will reach vulnerable communities.

Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed warned that the cost of climate damage competes with investment in essential services like schools and healthcare. Other African nations, including Côte d’Ivoire, Seychelles, Rwanda, and Zimbabwe, also highlighted their struggles with climate finance and adaptation at the COP31 Leaders’ Summit in Antalya.

lr.headline: Senator seeks US$5M for Grand Kru solar power
lr.dek: Grand Kru County Senator Numene T. H. Bartekwa urged the Senate to allocate funds for solar electricity in five major communities.
paragraphs: Grand Kru County Senator Numene T. H. Bartekwa asked the Liberian Senate on Thursday, November 12, to allocate US$5 million in the Fiscal Year 2027 National Budget for solar electricity in five major communities. Bartekwa stated that Grand Kru is excluded from the government's electricity expansion program, which is active in the other 14 counties. He warned that this exclusion impacts residents and businesses.

The senator said county officials and the Rural and Renewable Energy Agency (RREA) are exploring solar power as a cost-effective solution. RREA estimates US$1 million per community for mini-solar grids, totaling the US$5 million request for Barclayville, Grandcess, Buah Geeken, Sasstown, and Garaway. RREA has assured readiness to build similar systems to the one in Totota, Bong County, if funding is secured.

Bartekwa argued that the lack of electricity contradicts the government’s ARREST Agenda for Inclusive Development. He noted that while other counties receive electricity infrastructure, Grand Kru residents rely on expensive generators. He appealed to Senate Plenary to direct budget committees to consider the allocation during budget deliberations.

lr.headline: Liberia charges seven people over attack on police officer in Sinkor
lr.dek: Officer Sedeke K. Kammara reportedly lost use of an eye and had his radio, cap and US$150 taken during the assault
paragraphs: The Liberia National Police has arrested seven people and sent them to court over the alleged assault of a police officer and obstruction of officers in Sinkor, Monrovia. The suspects are Yokie Johnson, Rachel Johnson, Obediah Yorkor, Anthony Hallie, Spencil Z. Gaye, Prince Sackie and Harris Clomo.

The police said Officer Sedeke K. Kammara was attacked by a group from the beachside while responding to a situation on 26th Street, behind ERA Supermarket, on Thursday, November 12. Two officers of the Liberia Drug Enforcement Agency were with him but reportedly left the scene during the confrontation. The attackers allegedly injured his right eye and took his police-issued radio, face cap and US$150 in cash.

The seven face charges of aggravated assault, hindering law enforcement, physical obstruction of government functions, theft of property and disorderly conduct under Liberia's Revised Penal Law. The suspects are presumed innocent until the prosecution proves the allegations in court. The police condemned attacks on officers and said those suspected of breaking the law will be held accountable.

lr.headline: Benoni Urey named Liberia's seat on ECOWAS Business Council
lr.dek: The advisory body, chaired by Aliko Dangote, is meant to give the private sector a direct line to West Africa's presidents.
paragraphs: Benoni W. Urey, a Liberian businessman and founding shareholder of the mobile network Lonestar Cell MTN, has been named Liberia's representative on the ECOWAS Business Council. The council is a new advisory body chaired by Nigerian industrialist Aliko Dangote, Africa's richest man.

Ministers created the council on paper in 2021, but its launch slipped from December 2024 to September 2025. Dangote was named its first chairman by the bloc's foreign ministers in Abuja in December 2025, and West African heads of state later endorsed him.

Liberia trades heavily with Sierra Leone, Guinea and Côte d'Ivoire and imports almost all of its fuel. Whether the seat delivers cheaper fuel, easier border crossings and a bigger market for Liberian goods will depend on how hard its representative fights for a small country in the room.

ly.headline: Libya presents climate plans at COP31
ly.dek: Minister Mohamed Sidi Ibrahim presented national documents on mitigation and adaptation in Antalya, Turkey.
paragraphs: Libya's Minister of Environment, Mohamed Sidi Ibrahim, presented the country's climate change mitigation and adaptation plans at the 31st Conference of the Parties (COP31) in Antalya, Turkey, on Friday. The presentation included Libya's First National Communication, National Adaptation Plan, and Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC) document.

The documents were prepared by the Ministry of Environment with support from the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ). Minister Ibrahim stressed the need to move from planning to implementing practical projects and called for coordinated efforts among state institutions and stronger international cooperation.

The conference in Turkey runs from November 9 to 20. Minister of Oil and Gas, Khalifa Abdel-Sadig, and Minister of Water Resources, Hosni Owaidan, were also present at the presentation alongside UN and international officials.

mg.headline: Madagascar requisitions Enelec power plant
mg.dek: The government takes control of the Enelec fuel oil plant in Toamasina for up to 24 months, with the final cost and scope yet to be determined.
paragraphs: The Malagasy government has requisitioned Enelec's fuel oil power plant in Toamasina, transferring operational control to the state-owned utility JIRAMA. A decree dated November 3 placed the plant and its operational resources under state control, excluding solar power, for a maximum of 24 months. The exact financial implications, including who will cover fuel, salaries, maintenance, and potential compensation, remain unclear.

This measure follows a period of recurring power outages in Antananarivo and Toamasina. While new turbines in the capital had temporarily reduced cuts in late 2025, power disruptions returned by November 5 due to issues at the Andekaleka plant. In Toamasina, cyclone Gezani damaged the network in early 2026, and Enelec's plant was operating at only 30% capacity.

The state's action is authorized by the Electricity Code in cases of service disruption. JIRAMA will now manage the plant's operations and can directly purchase maintenance parts. The Enelec personnel will remain in place under JIRAMA's direction, with reports indicating JIRAMA will contribute to salaries. The transfer of control does not include ownership of the company.

mg.headline: Randrianasoloniaiko remains head of National Assembly
mg.dek: Vice-president denies rumors of a move to oust the permanent bureau, citing normal legislative work.
paragraphs: Rumors of a leadership change at Madagascar's National Assembly have been denied by Fanomezantsoa Andrianjanahary, the institution's vice-president. Andrianjanahary stated on Thursday, November 12, that no initiative to remove the permanent bureau was underway, aiming to quell speculation circulating on social media about internal crisis. Legislative activities, including the examination of the 2027 finance bill, continue normally, with deputies from the Vondron'ny Fihavaozan'i Madagasikara (VFM) maintaining their support for the current president, Siteny Randrianasoloniaiko.

The denial comes amid reports of a low parliamentary presence during budget sessions, which Andrianjanahary attributed to deputies visiting their constituencies to present their work. Despite these assurances, Randrianasoloniaiko's political positioning has raised questions, particularly his reduced public communication compared to earlier stages of the current administration. This shift fuels speculation about a potential cooling of relations with Colonel Michaël Randrianirina, though no verified information confirms a dispute between them.

Randrianasoloniaiko played a decisive role in the current power structure, having approached the High Constitutional Court prior to the October 14, 2025, decision that tasked Colonel Michaël Randrianirina with presidential duties. The National Assembly itself experienced a significant leadership change on October 15, 2025, when 127 deputies voted to remove the previous permanent bureau. Currently, no similar scenario is anticipated, with the existing bureau maintaining its functions and the 2027 budget review officially prioritized.

mg.headline: Photographer killed in Andraharo road accident
mg.dek: A taxi-ville driver who fled the scene was arrested by police early Friday, and tested above the legal alcohol limit.
paragraphs: A 28-year-old photographer named Faneva died on Thursday evening in Andraharo, Antananarivo, after a taxi-ville struck his motorcycle near Cap 3000 at about 7:30 PM. The taxi driver fled toward Tsarasaotra, and witnesses who tried to chase him did not catch him.

Police from the public security station of the capital's Fifth arrondissement took the badly injured rider to the Joseph Ravoahangy-Andrianavalona University Hospital Centre (HJRA), where doctors could only confirm his death. His body was placed in the hospital morgue. Investigators identified the taxi quickly, and the 45-year-old driver was arrested at about 5:30 AM on Friday and placed in custody. Early findings indicate his blood alcohol level was above the legal limit.

On the same evening, another motorcyclist died on the bypass between Ambohitrimanjaka and the Andranotapahana road exit after being hit by a 4x4. On Friday morning at about 7:30 AM, a pedestrian crossing at a zebra crossing in Ankorondrano was knocked down by a motorcycle, and the rider was seriously hurt. The exact circumstances and responsibilities for the first crash are still to be established by the investigation.

paragraphs: Malawians in Lilongwe, Blantyre, Zomba and Mzuzu are expected to take to the streets on November 17 to protest growing economic hardship. The complaints centre on fuel shortages, electricity blackouts and a scarcity of foreign exchange.

The fuel shortage, now in its 10th week, has left motorists queuing for hours at filling stations and pushed up fares and commodity prices, according to the commentary. Importers struggle to access dollars, and manufacturers find it hard to get raw materials.
Organisers describe peaceful demonstrations as a constitutional right and urge the government to listen rather than dismiss the protests as politically motivated.

mw.headline: Health groups demand fair recruitment
mw.dek: Malawi's health sector faces a critical recruitment drive from November 20 to 22, with advocacy groups pushing for transparency.
paragraphs: Two health advocacy organisations, the Malawi Health Equity Network (MHEN) and the Universal Health Coverage Coalition (UHCC), are demanding a fair and transparent recruitment process for health workers. The exercise, scheduled for November 20 to 22, 2026, aims to strengthen the country's health workforce. MHEN and UHCC have urged the government to prevent favouritism and political interference, ensuring all candidates have an equal opportunity.

The organisations welcomed the recruitment drive as a chance to improve healthcare delivery but called for measures to prevent overcrowding and ensure candidate safety during interviews. They specifically requested that serving health workers who have upgraded their qualifications be given a fair chance to compete for senior positions matching their new skills and experience. A strictly merit-based process, free from unfair treatment, is essential for boosting staff morale and career progression.

MHEN and UHCC stressed that a transparent recruitment process promotes equal opportunities and strengthens healthcare delivery. mw.headline: Malawi wins African Court case against Tsaperas
mw.dek: The African Court on Human and Peoples’ Rights dismissed a K233 billion compensation claim against Malawi.
paragraphs: Malawi has won a significant legal battle at the African Court on Human and Peoples’ Rights, with the court throwing out a K233 billion (US$133.7 million) compensation claim against the country. Attorney General Frank Mbeta confirmed the victory in Arusha, Tanzania, following the ruling.

The case involved South African businessman Patroklos Tsaperas and stemmed from the collapse of a telecommunications deal with Malawi Mobile Limited (MML), a company in which Tsaperas is a shareholder. MML was granted a mobile phone licence in 2002 but failed to launch services within 12 months, leading regulators to revoke the licence in 2005.

Malawi’s High Court had previously awarded MML US$66.85 million in damages in 2012. This latest ruling spares Malawian taxpayers from a potentially massive financial payout after more than two decades of legal proceedings.

mw.headline: Egypt thrash Malawi 5-0 in Afcon qualifier
mw.dek: Malawi's Flames conceded five goals in Cairo, exposing defensive and midfield frailties.
paragraphs: Egypt defeated Malawi 5-0 in a 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifier in Cairo on Friday, November 13, 2026. Nasser Maher opened the scoring in the sixth minute, followed by Omar Marmoush in the tenth and Mohamed Hany in the 39th. Mohamed Salah added two more goals, one from a penalty in stoppage time, to complete the rout.

The Flames conceded two goals within the first 10 minutes, disrupting their tactical plan. Egypt's technical players controlled the midfield tempo, while Malawi struggled with physical presence and winning second balls. Richard Mbulu tested Egypt's goalkeeper in the 22nd minute, but his effort was saved. Coach Kalisto Pasuwa stated, "We made mistakes and we were punished. We respected them too much and ended up conceding too many goals."

Malawi's qualification hopes for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations are now in doubt following the heavy defeat. The team struggled to combine and support their striker in the final third. Pasuwa made five changes to the lineup that faced Angola, but the reshuffle failed to contain Egypt's pace and movement.

ml.headline: Inheritance disputes leave widows and orphans in Mali without their share
ml.dek: Relatives of deceased heads of family are reportedly sharing out property in disregard of the rights of widows and children.
paragraphs: In Mali, the death of a family head often leaves a painful gap, and in some households it brings a further hardship: widows and their children are denied their share of the inheritance. Relatives of the deceased are reportedly dividing his property while ignoring the rights of the widow and the orphans.

Studio Tamani asked why these practices are spreading and what remains of the values of solidarity, honour and responsibility that families have long relied on. The question was put to the traditionalist Sidiki Kouyaté on the Club Tamani programme, broadcast on 13 November 2026.
The same report, carried by Bamada.net, said the programme examined why inheritance has become a source of family division. It gave no figures on how many families are affected.

ml.headline: Niger bans peanut exports, with exceptions possible for Mali
ml.dek: The ban, set by an order dated 11 November, is meant to supply Niger's cooking-oil processing plants with local raw material.
paragraphs: Niger has banned the export of peanuts under order No. 05-18, dated 11 November 2026. Commerce and Industry Minister Abdoulaye Seydou announced the measure on Friday 13 November, saying it is intended to support local processing units, especially those that make cooking oil.

Exports to Mali remain possible in principle. Exceptional authorisations may be granted for shipments to countries of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES), but these follow a defined procedure and are not automatic. Seydou said illegal export attempts will lead to the seizure of the quantities concerned for the state, under the existing judicial procedure.

Peanuts join millet, paddy rice, sorghum and maize, whose exports were already banned. Seydou also reminded officials that public administrations must buy Nigerien-made products when they are available on the national market.
